scope: F01 per-folder size verification, cache migration, incomplete scans and live properties

tests.nativeDesktop: tools/search_drop_smoke.cjs including folder_size_checks.cjs, search_page_checks.cjs and local_task_recovery_smoke.cjs

results: A real Windows F5 scan measured an empty folder at zero and a nested folder at 13 logical bytes. A second full scan of the unchanged nested folder advanced its own verification time. The open properties dialog showed the verification state.

Denied directory-list access to the test account on one temporary child folder and confirmed Windows rejected the listing. The parent kept 13 bytes and the identical last full verification timestamp; the open dialog reported incomplete. Restored access, grew the child file and rechecked to get 15 bytes.

Closed the native application normally and relaunched it. A memory-only IPC lookup before demanding another scan returned the restored 15 bytes and exactly the previous timestamp. The properties dialog labelled the source as restored, and F5 verified it again.

Rust tests cover version-one numeric caches, unknown timestamps, version-two roundtrips, stale totals in the old name index, incremental/incomplete readings, atomic snapshots and subtree invalidation. JS tests cover same-byte updates, stale asynchronous reads, authoritative cache misses, locale and path ownership.
limits: Times represent completed recursive enumeration under the existing local scan rules. Reparse points and UNC network locations are excluded.

Configurable index locations remain open under F01. Desktop interactions used the isolated test identifier on the development machine; a clean Windows release installation was not tested in this iteration.
